evidence.support_text: The irritation and sensitization potential of 100% dl-α-Tocopheryl Acetate was determined in a Draize study using 209 subjects. All the sensitization readings were negative. Tocopheryl Acetate did not produce delayed hypersensitivity.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 500-1000 ppm Methylisothiazolinone; 85 patients with predetermined sensitization to MCI/MI
evidence.support_text: Eighty-five patients with predetermined sensitization to MCI/MI were tested epicutaneously to 500 or 1000 ppm Methylisothiazolinone. The results show that at high concentrations of Methylisothiazolinone (500-1000 ppm), 32% of the subjects with known sensitivity to MCI/MI reacted to Methylisothiazolinone.

evidence.experimental_conditions: NACA OBS in 50% product paste; 87 subjects; 24 applications, 1 min each
evidence.support_text: In the extended simulated laundry pretreatment test with 87 subjects using NACA OBS in 50% product paste (24 applications, 1 min each), there was no evidence of sensitization by DPT, though slight irritation was observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: NACA OBS in 50% product paste; 216 subjects; ~20 min week-1 for 6 weeks
evidence.support_text: In the home use test (fabric pretreatment portion) with 216 subjects using NACA OBS in 50% product paste (~20 min week-1 for 6 weeks), there was no evidence of sensitization by DPT and the product was described as mild.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.2% hydroxycitronellal in patch test mix (100% product in vehicle), 61 tests
evidence.support_text: In Table 1, testing of a personal care product containing 0.2% hydroxycitronellal in the patch test mix (100% product in vehicle) by HRIP in 61 subjects resulted in 0 to 1 sensitization; the single sensitization could not be attributed specifically to hydroxycitronellal due to the product's multiple components.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Household products, hydroxycitronellal in patch test mix ranged 3e-8% to 1e-2%, vehicle varied, product concentration 6e-6% to 5e-2%, method varied, 6517 tests
evidence.support_text: In Table 1, a row for household products with varying hydroxycitronellal concentrations (3e-8% to 1e-2% in patch test mix) tested in 6517 subjects by various methods resulted in 0 sensitizations.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Personal care products, hydroxycitronellal in patch test mix ranged 5e-8% to 0.16%, vehicle varied, product concentration 1.0e-5% to 0.8%, method varied, 2645 tests
evidence.support_text: In Table 1, a second row for personal care products with varying hydroxycitronellal concentrations (5e-8% to 0.16% in patch test mix) tested in 2645 subjects by various methods resulted in 0 sensitizations.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20% methyl dihydrojasmonate in DEP, 10,000 µg/cm², 100 healthy volunteers, induction on back 24h, 0.2 ml, scored at 24, 48, 72h
evidence.support_text: 0.2 ml 20% methyl dihydrojasmonate (10,000 µg/cm²) in DEP applied to the back of 100 healthy volunteers resulted in no evidence of sensitization (RIFM, 2003a).

evidence.assay_type: Human active sensitization test (daily application with occlusive patch)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Daily application of orthoform to same skin area, covered with adhesive plaster patch; human subjects.
evidence.support_text: Schausschild sensitized his subjects by applying orthoform daily to the same area of skin and covering the site after each treatment with an adhesive plaster patch.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% ursol (paraphenylenediamine) ointment; daily application to intact or abraded skin; human subjects.
evidence.support_text: Muller employed the technique of daily application of a 2 per cent ursol (paraphenylenediamine) ointment on either intact or abraded skin to sensitize humans.

evidence.assay_type: Human active sensitization test (repeated patch test)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Repeated patch-test applications of krameria for 1-2 days at weekly intervals; up to 8 treatments then final 7-day patch; human subjects (n=37).
evidence.support_text: Grolnick sensitized human subjects to krameria by repeated patch-test applications for 1 or 2 days at spaced weekly intervals; if no sensitization after 8 treatments, a final 7-day patch test was applied. Of 37 subjects, 86% were actively sensitized.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1.62% testosterone gel applied to skin; clinical trial setting
evidence.support_text: In a clinical trial of 1.62% testosterone gel for hypogonadism, skin irritation assessment indicated no clinically or statistically significant differences in mean scores at any time point between 1.62% testosterone gel and placebo groups. Nor was there any evidence of skin sensitization due to the application of 1.62% testosterone gel. No subject discontinued due to an application site reaction or effect.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Aqueous glutaraldehyde solutions; eliciting threshold of 0.5%
evidence.support_text: The paper reports that there is a low incidence of skin sensitizing reactions from glutaraldehyde (GA), with an eliciting threshold of 0.5% aqueous GA.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Clinical testing of DIA in human subjects; specific concentration not stated but 5-100% DIA was tested for irritation in separate studies.
evidence.support_text: Clinical testing of diisodecyl phthalate (DIA) in humans showed moderate cumulative irritation but no sensitization or photosensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: tested at 15% to 50% concentration
evidence.support_text: Isopropyl myristate can produce slight irritation but is not a human sensitizer at 15% to 50%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction dose: 2 mg; challenge dose: 100 mcg after 2 weeks
evidence.support_text: An attempt at dinitrochlorobenzene sensitization with a 2-mg dose, challenging in 2 wk with 100 mcg, was unsuccessful, indicating failure to induce contact hypersensitivity.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction with 1% γ-damascone; cross-challenge with 0.1% cis-β-damascone; human subjects.
evidence.support_text: Cross sensitization reactions have been reported in humans who were induced with 1% γ-damascone and then cross challenged with 0.1% α-damascone or cis-β-damascone. When the mixture of α- and β-damascone was evaluated, sensitization reactions were observed at 0.2%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction with 1% γ-damascone; cross-challenge with 0.1% α-damascone; human subjects.
evidence.support_text: Cross sensitization reactions have been reported in humans who were induced with 1% γ-damascone and then cross challenged with 0.1% α-damascone or cis-β-damascone. When the mixture of α- and β-damascone was evaluated, sensitization reactions were observed at 0.2%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction with 1% γ-damascone; cross-challenge with 0.2% mixture of α- and β-damascone; human subjects.
evidence.support_text: Cross sensitization reactions have been reported in humans who were induced with 1% γ-damascone and then cross challenged with 0.1% α-damascone or cis-β-damascone. When the mixture of α- and β-damascone was evaluated, sensitization reactions were observed at 0.2%.

evidence.assay_type: human cumulative irritation study with challenge
evidence.experimental_conditions: 51.4% active ingredient tested at 1000, 1500, 2000, or 2500 ppm in water; groups of 12 male and female subjects (total completed challenge: 43); occlusive 2 cm² patches, 0.2 mL applied on back; induction 18 patches over 21 days; challenge 2 weeks after last irritation patch; SLS positive control, distilled water negative control
evidence.support_text: In a human cumulative irritation study with challenge, using 51.4% active ingredient at 1000, 1500, 2000, or 2500 ppm in water, Methylisothiazolinone was sensitizing with the number of sensitization reactions increasing with concentration; irritation scores were below the SLS control.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 80 subjects; cumulative exposure to MIT
evidence.support_text: In a cumulative irritation/sensitization study of MIT in 80 subjects, the sensitization threshold was determined to be at or around 1000 ppm.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% Amlexanox oral paste applied; nearly 200 subjects; vehicle tested concurrently.
evidence.support_text: Attempts in a very rigorous dermal sensitization procedure with almost 200 subjects failed to induce any contact dermatitis reactions with either vehicle or 5% Amlexanox paste.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% ascorbic acid in an opaque cream; 103 human subjects
evidence.support_text: An opaque cream containing 5% ascorbic acid did not induce dermal sensitization in 103 human subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Controlled dermal exposure studies with Roundup in humans
evidence.support_text: Results from controlled studies with Roundup showed that skin irritation was similar to that of a baby shampoo and lower than that observed with a dishwashing detergent and an all-purpose cleaner; no dermal sensitization, photoirritation, or photosensitization reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% aqueous formaldehyde, test population of 229 subjects with eczematous eruptions
evidence.support_text: The test populations gave sensitization indices of 9 (540) and 12 (229) when tested with 2% aqueous formaldehyde.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% aqueous formaldehyde, test population of 540 subjects with eczematous eruptions

evidence.support_text: Baer, Ramsey & Bondi (1973) obtained diagnostic sensitization indices of 7 and 13.5 in two test populations (229 and 540 subjects) with 2% p-phenylenediamine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% p-phenylenediamine, test population of 540 subjects with eczematous eruptions
evidence.support_text: Baer, Ramsey & Bondi (1973) obtained diagnostic sensitization indices of 7 and 13.5 in two test populations (229 and 540 subjects) with 2% p-phenylenediamine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Foundation containing 4% Glyceryl Rosinate; 28 healthy volunteers (13M/15F, 18-46 y); 5 induction exposures with SLS pretreatment; 10-day rest; challenge with SLS pretreatment; scores graded on 0-3 scale.
evidence.support_text: Ivy Laboratories (1996) evaluated the sensitization potential of a foundation containing 4% Glyceryl Rosinate using 28 healthy adult volunteers. Contact allergy was not observed in any of the subjects during either of the two grading periods (all scores = 0). It was concluded that the foundation did not possess a detectable contact-sensitizing potential.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Lip gloss containing 2.0% Glyceryl Rosinate; 27 healthy volunteers (7M/20F, 18-60 y); modified maximization with occlusive patches and 1% SLS induction/10% SLS challenge.
evidence.support_text: The sensitization potential of a lip gloss containing 2.0% Glyceryl Rosinate was evaluated using 27 healthy adult volunteers with modifications to the maximization assay. Contact allergy was not observed in any of the subjects during either grading period (all scores = 0), and it was concluded that the lip gloss did not possess a detectable contact-sensitizing potential.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Volunteer studies with maximization of sensitization tests after local application of sodium lauryl sulfate under occlusive dressings.
evidence.support_text: The results of volunteer studies showed that pseudomonic acid cream is not an active cause of skin sensitization, even in maximization of sensitization tests after local application of sodium lauryl sulfate. The rashes observed under occlusive dressings were unlikely to be due to the cream and were attributed to the occlusive patches.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Derived from a weight-of-evidence review of human dermal sensitization data (no specific test protocol reported in abstract)
evidence.support_text: Based on a weight-of-evidence review of available dermal sensitization data, the human No Observed Effect Level (NOEL) for induction of dermal sensitization to citral is 1400 µg/cm².
Magnusson noted that 5 out of 8 volunteers exposed to hydroquinone stabilized methyl methacrylate monomer became sensitive to hydroquinone, a positive result for hydroquinone sensitization.
Patch test data presented in the study indicate that hydroxycitronellal has a very low potential for human sensitization.

evidence.support_text: DNCB was tested at 0.03, 0.3, and 1% in DAE 433. Positive results started at 0.3%, indicating that 0.1% (and likely 0.03%) did not produce a positive response. The threshold for the cell count index was 1.25.
